summary: Douglas County lookout on Lookout Mountain, Umpqua NF: 1924 D-6 cupola cabin, 1949 30-foot L-4 tower, abandoned 1966, removed or destroyed 1983; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 30-foot timber tower with an L-4 cab (1949), after a D-6 cupola cabin (1924)
facts.status_note: Removed in 1983 per the register; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1983; no source describes what remains
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umpqua National Forest

events.note: Harry Willis returned to his station for further duty (News-Review, Nov 26, 1936)
30-foot timber tower with an L-4 cab and cabin
Abandoned per register and firelookout.com; a 1972 letter describes recent use
Letter tied to a July 5, 1972 inspection: emergency lookout about four days a season, $1,000-$1,500 repairs, recommended disposal
Register says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed

evidence.quote: There was a D-6 cupola ground-cabin constructed in 1924.

evidence.supports: L-4 tower and cabin built 1949, abandoned 1966
evidence.quote: The L-4 tower and cabin were built in 1949 and abandoned in 1966.
1924: D-6 cupola cabin. 1949: 30' wooden L-4 tower.

evidence.supports: location on the Umpqua National Forest, about 30 miles east of Roseburg
1949 30-foot timber tower with an L-4 cab
evidence.quote: 1949: A 30-foot timber tower with an L-4 cab constructed

corrections.proposed: 30-foot L-4 tower with cab (1949); D-6 describes the earlier 1924 cupola cabin
corrections.why: D-6 is the 1924 ground cupola cabin; the structure built in 1949 is recorded as an L-4 tower and cab

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and firelookout.com give abandonment in 1966; a July 5, 1972 letter describes the lookout as used about four days a season, so the 1966 date does not match that use. The story reports both.
Register says removed in 1983; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1983. Both agree on the year.

notes_for_editor: Brief design D-6 is only the 1924 cupola cabin; the proposed correction gives the 1949 L-4 tower. The 1966 abandonment date conflicts with the 1972 letter describing use; the story reports both. No source describes the site today. The register photo captions (1948, 1956) have no image URLs in the fetched text, so no photos are added.
